newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima says Austria must make EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima says Austria must make EMU start.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Tuesday Austria was on track to qualify for a single European currency and warned that failure to participate would spell disaster for the nation's economy.
"Not to take part in (European) Economic and Monetary Union would be a catastrophe for our economy," Klima said in a statement issued by the Social Democratic Party.
The Maastricht criteria governing interest rates, inflation, exchange rates and the deficit quota made good economic sense, he said.
A single European currency would create stability and cut out the risks associated with exchange rate fluctuations, he continued.
"We cannot prevent EMU, we have to join in," Klima said, reiterating his opposition to softening the Maastricht criteria or postponing the single currency's start date beyond 1999.
He said the government's 1996 and 1997 budgets had put Austria "well on the way" to making the grade for European Economic and Monetary Union.
